title: Rate of Reaction
seo_title: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: Rate of Reaction Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: Rate and extent of reaction
standard_text: Reaction rate as the change in concentration (or mass, or volume) per unit time; factors that affect the rate: nature of reactants, concentration (pressure), surface area, temperature and catalysts; collision theory; the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution; measuring rates of reaction. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 12, Chemistry: Rate and extent of reaction)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): reaction rate, factors that affect rate, collision theory, activation energy, catalysts and measuring rates. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Only collisions with enough energy and the right orientation are effective.
body_html:
How to think about it

Collision theory: particles must collide with enough energy (at least the activation energy) and with the correct orientation for a reaction to happen. The rate increases if collisions happen more often or more of them are effective.

Higher concentration or pressure and larger surface area give more collisions per second. A higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, so more of them have enough energy to react (seen on a Maxwell–Boltzmann curve). A catalyst gives a pathway with a lower activation energy. Rates are measured by gas volume, mass loss or colour change.

Example

50 cm³ of gas forms in 25 s. Average rate?

volume ÷ time

Answer: 2 cm³·s⁻¹

Example

Why does powdered zinc react faster than a lump?

Surface area

Answer: it has a larger surface area, so there are more collisions

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a catalyst increases the energy of the particles.
  • Thinking a higher temperature only increases the number of collisions.
  • Thinking a catalyst changes the yield.

faq.a: The low temperature slows down the reactions that make food go off.

items.q: The reaction mixture is stirred constantly. What happens to the reaction rate?

items.q: A catalyst is added to N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub> (the Haber process) at equilibrium. What happens?
